stem: In which of the following states is black soil found?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Black soils are found over most parts of the Deccan Plateau. This includes parts of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. The largest extent of this soil is found in Maharashtra. Deep black soil occurs in the upper parts of the Godavari and Krishna river basins and in the north-western part of the Deccan Plateau. These soils are also called regur and cotton soil. Generally, black soils are deep, clayey, and impermeable. They swell and become sticky when wet, and shrink when dry. They are also known as self-ploughing soils. Due to slow absorption of moisture and low moisture loss, black soil retains moisture for a long period.

stem: Which one of the following soils is deposited by rivers?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Alluvial soil is formed from the silt deposited by rivers. Alluvial soils are divided into two sub-types— (1) new alluvium or Khadar: Khadar is formed in the river’s floodplain area, where a fresh layer of soil gets deposited every year during floods. (2) Old alluvium or Bhangar: This soil is found at some height away from the reach of floods.

stem: Old Kachhari clay of Gangetic plain is called
expl: The old alluvial soil of the Ganga plain is called Bangar. It is found at some height beyond the reach of floods. The colour of this soil is pale reddish brown.

stem: Soil water available to plants is maximum in :
expl: Clayey soil has the highest water-holding capacity. Therefore, plants get the maximum water in this soil. Clayey soil contains less than 50% silt, up to 50% clay, and some amount of sand. Air movement is low in it, which leads to waterlogging.

stem: In Soil, Water that is readily available to plant root is

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The roots of a tree get water from the soil in the form of capillary water. Capillary water remains stored in the fine pores of the soil. The water that forms the soil solution is loosely held around soil particles. Hence, the water available to plant roots in soil is capillary water.

stem: Which state has the most laterite soil?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Laterite soil develops in regions of high temperature and heavy rainfall. It is formed as a result of intense leaching caused by rainfall. This soil is mainly developed in the higher parts of the Peninsular Plateau. It is chiefly found in the hilly regions of Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, the plateau region of Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Odisha, and Assam.

stem: Which of the following soils are commonly used for bricks?
expl: Laterite soil is commonly used for making bricks. This soil contains a high proportion of iron and aluminium.

stem: Plants that grow in saline soil are called—
expl: Halophytes are those plants that grow in saline soil.

expl: Soil conservation includes all measures that protect soil from erosion and maintain its fertility. Important measures for preventing soil erosion include afforestation, terrace or contour farming, checking overgrazing and shifting cultivation, and bunding. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: Soil conservation is a process in which—

options.label: a
options.text: Infertile soil is converted into fertile soil

expl: In a broad sense, soil conservation does not mean only controlling soil erosion, but also maintaining a high level of land fertility. In general, the measures adopted to protect soil from damage and to conserve its fertility and health are known as soil conservation.
